stories.title: Implement typed Skyscanner API client
stories.description: Create src/skyscanner/client.ts that wraps the Skyscanner RapidAPI. The client must: (1) export a SkyscannerClient class whose constructor accepts { apiKey: string }; if apiKey is omitted, fall back to the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable — throw a descriptive Error if neither is present; (2) implement searchFlights(params: SearchParams): Promise<FlightResult[]> using the Node.js 18+ global fetch (no third-party HTTP library); (3) export TypeScript interfaces SearchParams { origin: string; destination: string; date: string; adults?: number } and FlightResult { price: number; currency: string; airline: string; departure: string; arrival: string; duration: number; stops: number }; (4) throw on HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, including the status code in the message; (5) throw a descriptive parse error when the response body does not match the expected shape. Also create src/skyscanner/client.test.ts with vitest tests that mock the global fetch — no real network calls. (6) Support an explicit mock mode: when the environment variable MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API is set to the exact string 'true', searchFlights must return deterministic fixture FlightResult[] data WITHOUT making any network call (no fetch invocation at all) — this is an opt-in-only behavior; when MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API is unset, empty, or any value other than 'true', searchFlights must behave exactly as it does today (real fetch call, real failures surfaced, no silent fallback to mock data on real-call failure).
acceptanceCriteria: src/skyscanner/client.ts exports a SkyscannerClient class whose constructor signature is constructor({ apiKey }: { apiKey?: string })
SearchParams interface is exported with exactly: origin: string, destination: string, date: string, adults?: number
FlightResult interface is exported with exactly: price: number, currency: string, airline: string, departure: string, arrival: string, duration: number, stops: number
searchFlights uses the Node.js global fetch exclusively — no axios, node-fetch, or other HTTP dependency imported
When no apiKey is passed to the constructor and RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is unset, constructing SkyscannerClient throws an Error whose message references the missing key
When the API returns a 4xx or 5xx status, searchFlights rejects with an Error that includes the HTTP status code
When the API response body is malformed or missing expected fields, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive parse/validation Error
The apiKey is stored as a private field (private or # prefix) on the SkyscannerClient instance and is not publicly readable
When apiKey is passed as an empty string ('') to the constructor, SkyscannerClient throws the same missing-key Error as when apiKey is omitted entirely
When RAPIDAPI_KEY is set to an empty string in the environment and no apiKey is provided to the constructor, SkyscannerClient throws the missing-key Error
When an apiKey is provided to the constructor and RAPIDAPI_KEY is also set in the environment, the constructor-provided apiKey takes precedence
The Error thrown by searchFlights on HTTP 4xx/5xx does not include the apiKey value anywhere in its message string
tsc --noEmit exits 0 with no type errors

A real HTTP/API failure (4xx, 5xx, network error, malformed body) is NEVER silently replaced with mock/fixture data — mock mode only ever activates via the explicit MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API='true' env var, never as an automatic fallback

stories.title: Implement flight search CLI entry point with formatted table output - Core Implementation
stories.description: Create `src/cli.ts` — a standalone Node entry point that accepts flight search arguments via `process.argv` and prints results as an aligned table. Parse flags manually (no commander, no yargs, zero new runtime deps). Require `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var; exit 1 with a human-readable message if absent. Instantiate `SkyscannerClient` from `src/skyscanner/client.ts` (SKY-002), call `searchFlights` forwarding all parsed arguments including adults count, and render results in a dynamically-padded table with columns: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops. Column widths are determined by the widest value in each column (including the header). A separator row of hyphen characters must appear between the header and data rows. Price is right-aligned and prefixed with the currency symbol returned by the API (default £ if absent); all other columns are left-aligned. If no flights are returned print `No flights found.` and exit 0. On any thrown error print the message to stderr and exit 1.
acceptanceCriteria: Delegated to split children: SKY-003-impl, SKY-003-test

stories.title: Build Express REST API with /health, /search, /cheapest, and static dashboard endpoints
stories.description: Create src/server.ts — an Express HTTP server that exposes: (1) GET /health → { status: 'ok', uptime: number }, (2) GET /search?from=LHR&to=JFK&date=2026-08-01&adults=1 → { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: string }, (3) GET /cheapest?from=LHR&to=JFK&date=2026-08-01 → the single cheapest FlightResult or 404 JSON { error: string } if none found, (4) GET / → serves src/public/index.html by reading the file at runtime (e.g. fs.readFileSync) — the handler must NOT hardcode a separate inline HTML string that merely happens to match; content and implementation must not be able to diverge. Server reads PORT from env (default 3000); reads RAPIDAPI_KEY from env and passes to SkyscannerClient. If RAPIDAPI_KEY is absent at startup all API routes (/search, /cheapest) return 503 { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; /health and / are never gated. The listen() call must be guarded so importing `app` in tests does not bind a port. Add 'start' script in package.json pointing to 'node dist/server.js'. Install supertest and @types/supertest. Create src/server.test.ts using vitest + supertest with at least 8 tests covering the scenarios in acceptance criteria. Depends on SKY-002 (SkyscannerClient and FlightResult type must exist before this story is started). The build script must copy src/public/ (or equivalent static assets) into dist/public/ as part of `npm run build`, since tsc alone does not copy non-.ts files — the file path used by the /  route handler must resolve correctly both under `tsx src/server.ts` (dev) and `node dist/server.js` (built).
acceptanceCriteria: src/server.ts exports a named `app` (Express instance) separately from the `listen()` call so supertest can import it without binding a port

The `listen()` call in src/server.ts is guarded by `import { pathToFileURL } from 'url'` and the condition `if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href)` (ESM output) or `if (require.main === module)` (CJS output) — the guard form must match the tsup output format so that `vitest run` never binds a port
GET /health returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and body matching { status: 'ok', uptime: <positive number> }
GET /health returns HTTP 200 regardless of whether RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is set or absent — the health endpoint is never gated by API key presence

GET / returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type matching text/html and response body equal to the contents of src/public/index.html, READ FROM THAT FILE AT RUNTIME (e.g. fs.readFileSync) — a hardcoded/duplicated inline HTML string in server.ts that happens to match is NOT acceptable; this route is never gated by RAPIDAPI_KEY

src/public/index.html exists and is a real, styled single-page dashboard (not a placeholder) matching this concrete layout: (1) a full-width solid-color header bar (e.g. blue #1a73e8) containing a bold white title 'Skyscanner Dashboard' and a smaller subtitle line below it ('Search flights via the Skyscanner API' or equivalent); (2) below the header, a centered white card (max-width ~700px, rounded corners, light border, padding) containing a search form laid out as a 2-column grid: 'From (IATA)' and 'To (IATA)' text inputs on row 1, 'Date' (native date input) and 'Adults' (number input, default 1) on row 2, each with a label above the input; (3) a full-width solid-color button below the grid, same color as the header, labeled 'Search Flights'; (4) a status/message area below the button that shows a light-red/pink banner with red text for errors (e.g. 'Failed to fetch flights'), a muted-gray line for empty results ('No flights found'), and a result count on success; (5) client-side JavaScript that submits the form via GET /search (no full page reload), disables the button while the request is in flight, and renders returned flights into a results table (or the appropriate status message) in the same page

GET /search with valid query params (from, to, date, adults) returns HTTP 200 with body { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: ISO-8601 string } where count strictly equals flights.length
GET /search missing any required param (from, to, or date) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }
When the `adults` query param is absent on GET /search, the request succeeds (HTTP 200) with a default value of 1 passed to SkyscannerClient — `adults` is optional, not required
When the `adults` query param is present but non-numeric (e.g. 'abc', ''), GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }

GET /cheapest with valid required query params (from, to, date) returns HTTP 200 with a single FlightResult whose `price` field is less than or equal to the `price` field of every FlightResult returned by SkyscannerClient for the same route/date (validated against a mocked client response); if `adults` is supplied it is forwarded, if absent it defaults to 1
GET /cheapest returns HTTP 404 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string } when SkyscannerClient returns an empty array for the given route/date
GET /cheapest missing any required param (from, to, or date) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }

When RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is absent at server initialisation, a single middleware (or equivalent) short-circuits GET /search and GET /cheapest with HTTP 503 Content-Type application/json body { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; GET /health and GET / are unaffected and return their normal responses

When SkyscannerClient throws an error during a /search or /cheapest request (e.g. network failure, upstream 5xx), the server returns HTTP 500 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string } and does not crash or emit an unhandled promise rejection

The `searchedAt` field in the GET /search response is an ISO-8601 datetime string reflecting the time of the request (not a hardcoded value); successive requests separated by at least 1 ms return distinct values

The FlightResult type used in src/server.ts is imported from the SKY-002 type export (e.g. src/skyscanner/client.ts) and not redeclared inline — type definitions must not diverge between the client and server layers

src/server.test.ts contains at least 8 vitest tests, each covering a distinct scenario from the criteria above, with SkyscannerClient mocked (vi.mock or equivalent) so no real HTTP calls are made during `vitest run`
`npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 with no type errors
`vitest run` exits 0 with all tests passing
The server handles the case where `src/public/index.html` is missing or unreadable in a graceful way, returning an HTTP 500 error with proper error message
The server sets appropriate CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS) for all routes except /health
All string literals in the server's response body are sanitized to prevent XSS vulnerabilities in the HTML response
The server sanitizes user-provided inputs to GET /search and GET /cheapest to prevent injection attacks, especially in the 'from' and 'to' IATA code fields
GET /search and GET /cheapest handle invalid 'date' values gracefully, by returning HTTP 400 with { error: string } that explains the invalid format
The server does not expose sensitive environment variables in error responses or logs
The server implements rate limiting for GET /search and GET /cheapest to prevent abuse (e.g. 10 requests per minute per IP)
GET /cheapest response includes a `cheapestPrice` field in the FlightResult which matches the lowest price among all returned flights

stories.title: Implement flight search CLI entry point core logic
stories.description: Create `src/cli.ts` — a standalone Node entry point that accepts flight search arguments via `process.argv` and prints results as an aligned table. Parse flags manually (no commander, no yargs, zero new runtime deps). Require `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var; exit 1 with a human-readable message if absent. Instantiate `SkyscannerClient` from `src/skyscanner/client.ts` (SKY-002), call `searchFlights` forwarding all parsed arguments including adults count, and render results in a dynamically-padded table with columns: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops. Column widths are determined by the widest value in each column (including the header). A separator row of hyphen characters must appear between the header and data rows. Price is right-aligned and prefixed with the currency symbol returned by the API (default £ if absent); all other columns are left-aligned. If no flights are returned print `No flights found.` and exit 0. On any thrown error print the message to stderr and exit 1.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/cli.ts` exists and `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors
`tsconfig.json` sets `outDir` to `dist` and emits a module format compatible with `node dist/cli.js` invocation (CommonJS or ESM with .mjs extension consistently applied)
Flags `--from`, `--to`, and `--date` are all required; if any is absent the CLI prints a usage hint to stderr (showing correct flag names) and exits with code 2
The `--date` flag value must match the pattern `YYYY-MM-DD`; a value that does not match this format causes exit code 2 with a human-readable message written to stderr before any network call is made
Optional `--adults` flag defaults to 1 when omitted; a non-integer value, a value ≤ 0, or a non-numeric string causes exit code 2 with a human-readable message to stderr
The parsed `adults` value is forwarded as an argument to `SkyscannerClient.searchFlights` — the flag is not silently dropped
If `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var is unset or empty, CLI prints 'Error: RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable is required' to stderr and exits 1 before making any network call

The compiled output must be invokable as `node dist/cli.js ...` after `tsc`; `tsconfig.json` must have `outDir` set to `dist` and emit CommonJS-compatible output.

All columns except Price are left-aligned within their padded width; the Price column is right-aligned within its padded width
Price column values are prefixed with the currency symbol from the API response; if the API response omits a currency symbol, £ is used as the fallback
When `searchFlights` resolves with an empty array, stdout contains exactly the line `No flights found.` and process exits 0
When `searchFlights` rejects, the error message is written to stderr and process exits 1; stdout is empty

GET /search with valid query params (from, to, date, adults) returns HTTP 200 with body { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: ISO-8601 string } where count strictly equals flights.length
GET /search missing any required param (from, to, or date) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }
